entries.title: Crypto Puzzles 2018: Puzzle #2
entries.series: Crypto Puzzles (2018 YouTube channel), same series as the solved Puzzle #1

author.name: unnamed, published under the YouTube channel "Crypto Puzzles"

prize.note: single externally-owned account, never signed a transaction (nonce 0); that this address is Puzzle #2's escrow is a strong inference from the funder and amount matching Puzzle #1, not stated directly by the author

entries.target_format: 64-character hex private key (32 bytes), secp256k1, Keccak-256 of the uncompressed public key to a 20-byte address, no BIP39, no passphrase, no derivation path

derivation.summary: read a 64-character hex private key hidden as composite glyphs across the two Puzzle #2 videos, then derive secp256k1 -> Keccak-256 -> last 20 bytes to an Ethereum address
derivation.certified_against: Puzzle #1's own published solution (64-hex answer read from its solution video), which derives to the address that received and was later spent from for that puzzle's own 0.05 ETH prize in 2018

entries.difficulty_note: 16 of 64 characters are recovered and reproduce across two independent codecs. Three independent lines suggest the remaining 48 were never published: Puzzle 2 contains no flash frames where Puzzle 1 used them for the bulk of its key, Part 1 spends a whole seam on redundancy, and a 2018 commenter reported the same 16 characters and asked for a next part that never came.

leads.title: the three coordinates address an 8x8 grid
the four screen edges specify four block transforms
identify the unattributed video clip in Part 2

entries.third_party_material: No video frames, screenshots, or video files are included; both puzzles are linked by video ID only. The certification vector (Puzzle #1's already-solved private key) is drawn from the author's own public solution video for a prize claimed and spent by an unrelated third party in 2018.

entries.title: Smith, Lyle & Moore Hunt #2: Glimmer

prize.note: 3,177,700 sats, funded in a single transaction on 2022-07-29, unspent

entries.target_format: BIP39 12 words, English wordlist, plus a passphrase, BIP84 m/84'/0'/0'/0/0, P2WPKH

derivation.summary: 12 BIP39 words plus a passphrase, scattered across 3 password-gated web pages, derived along BIP84 to a P2WPKH address matching the escrow; the author separately published the account xpub
derivation.certified_against: the published account xpub, whose m/0/0 P2WPKH address equals the escrow; a known-wrong BIP39 test vector is also confirmed to produce NO MATCH. The BIP39-mnemonic-to-seed leg has no known-good vector, since 0 of 12 words are held

entries.difficulty_note: the 12 words and passphrase are locked behind 3 password-gated pages, each requiring a specific author-intended answer to a riddle rather than a decodable cipher; about 5,000 candidates have been tried across the 3 locks with 0 hits, none of them a certified exhaustive negative

tested_total.note: no research in this catalogue; see open-crypto-puzzles for prior work

sources.title: Smith, Lyle & Moore, Treasure Hunt page

entries.third_party_material: no Wix page mirrors, no audio/video files, no Instagram media shipped; only 3 short verbatim riddle quotes (about 220 words total) with the site URL, and my own derived structure/pipeline data

entries.title: Zden Level HALV
entries.target_format: 256-bit private key as direct hex, P2PKH

derivation.summary: read the 256 quaternary levels off the waveform lattice, reduce 512 raw bits to a 256-bit key by a rule not yet identified, derive P2PKH and compare to the escrow
derivation.certified_against: a positive control key generated in the same run, plus an assertion that the target is HALV and not the sibling LVL5 puzzle, whose hash160 shares its first four bytes

entries.difficulty_note: the 256 levels are exact and confirmed by two independent fitting objectives; what is missing is the rule reducing 512 raw bits to 256. No hint has been published for this puzzle, unlike others in the series.

entries.title: Zden Cryptopuzzle LVL.5
entries.target_format: 256-bit private key as direct hex (not WIF, not BIP39), P2PKH

derivation.summary: sum the areas of 2 'following' rectangles (of 64 in an 8x8 grid) under a formula read from a pixel-level hint, normalize to 1 byte, repeat for 32 byte pairs to build a 256-bit private key, derive P2PKH and compare to the escrow
derivation.certified_against: a standard public vector, private key 1 (the generator point); the puzzle's own rectangle-to-key reading is not itself certified

entries.difficulty_note: geometry is fully measured, including two border channels that public readings discard. Two deductions narrow the formula: no linear encoding of a pair sum exists, and a literal divide by 64 cannot reach byte range for any area definition. The 2021 correction marks act on the inner rectangle, excluding outer-area-only formulas.

leads.title: a clarification from the author on 3 exact bindings (x, byte-range normalization, following)
a higher-fidelity source for the mini-hint glyphs
a wider author-error tolerance sweep (3-byte wildcard)
